page.h1: HTS Chapter 52: Cotton — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Chapter 52 Export Markets: Tariffs on U.S. Cotton by Country
seo.shortDescription: The tariff each top buyer charges on U.S. raw cotton, yarn and fabric, with the trade agreement and plant-health regulator for each.

intro: For raw cotton, tariffs are close to zero in most markets: Viet Nam charges 0% on cotton fiber (USDA, April 2026), and Mexico, Honduras, the Dominican Republic and Guatemala are duty-free under USMCA or CAFTA-DR. China is the one buyer that costs real money, at a 1% in-quota or 40% out-of-quota rate plus 10% on every U.S. good. India's normal 11% duty has been waived on and off. For Pakistan, Türkiye and Bangladesh an official 2026 duty rate was not confirmed, so those cells say so rather than guess.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

assumptions: Rates come from USDA Foreign Agricultural Service cotton reports (Viet Nam, China, April 2026), the trade agreements (USMCA, CAFTA-DR) and India's Ministry of Textiles release of August 2025. Where no official 2026 figure was found, the cell says 'not individually verified'.

One representative group stands in for each of the three kinds of goods: raw cotton (5201–5203), yarn (5204–5207) and woven fabric (5208–5212). Yarn and fabric are 18% of the chapter, so their rates matter less than raw cotton's.

India's duty is shown as 11% (5% basic duty plus 5% AIDC cess, plus a 10% surcharge on both) with the waiver periods the Ministry of Textiles announced; the 2026 waiver is reported in the press and was not confirmed from the official notification.
Taxes that are not tariffs, such as value-added and sales taxes, are the buyer's business and are not shown.
National 8–10-digit tariff lines can set a different rate than the group shown here — check the market's own schedule before relying on this page for a transaction.
